scope: Fresh zero-authorship native verification of Settings HTTP Forget retry after rejected Chrome storage.remove, Reset Cancel, and remaining-control corpus across guest/member/admin.

artifact.kind: CI development artifact, not published Store or real desktop engine

verdict_a.observed: Each role opened the actual headed extension Settings side panel with identity verified. The disposable HTTP availability fixture exposed the product Forget control. Cancel retained the owned pair code. A rejected Chrome storage.remove left the code intact and showed a retry error; the next trusted UI confirmation removed that stored code and cleared the error. Reset Cancel preserved every baseline local/session value; the corpus also passed port boundaries/filter/blank-clear, reset refusal/retry, reload, and signed-out state.
limitations: HTTP transport was announced by a disposable availability message; actual desktop engine pairing acceptance, connection, and rediscovery were not verified.
Full T43–T51 criteria and public Store build/release acceptance remain partial; D84 persistence closure decision belongs to coordinator.

findings: Observed pair removal and error state come from live chrome.storage.local and visible Settings DOM; the fault wrapper is installed only at Chrome storage.remove, with one rejected call asserted and then restored before retry. A no-op product Forget handler cannot pass the stored-code removal check.
Reset Cancel is clicked through the native pointer driver and is followed by exact hashed-value comparison for every prior local/session entry; a skipped or destructive Cancel fails.
Corrected nondigit oracle expects rendered 123 after typing 12x3; pane-scoped Forget selector resolves prior ambiguity, while dialog confirmation stays scoped. No production source changed.
The injected HTTP availability fixture is only a UI exposure mechanism and cannot establish real engine behavior.
